You can export and import JSON input files from the System Advisor Model (SAM) Software Development Kit (SDK) using SAM's built-in Code Generator.When using SAM's Code Generator, you can choose between two primary JSON output formats:When using SAM's Code Generator, you can choose between two primary JSON output formats:PySAM JSON Option: Exports a separate JSON file for each individual compute module required by your configuration (e.g., <case>_pvwattsv8.json, <case>_grid.json). This structure maps directly to modular objects in Python via PySAM Documentation.JSON for Inputs Option: Exports all configuration inputs into a single combined JSON file.How to Generate a JSON Input File in SAMOpen your project/case inside the System Advisor Model desktop app.Go to Simulate or open the Code Generator tool.Select the target language or output option (PySAM JSON or JSON for Inputs).Choose a destination folder on your computer to save the generated JSON file(s) and supporting SDK files (ssc.dll, sscapi.h, etc.).How to Load and Use JSON Inputs in PySAM (Python)To read a JSON file and load the values into a PySAM model:To read a JSON file and load the values into a PySAM model:Using PySAM JSON (Per-Module Files):pythonimport json
import PySAM.Pvwattsv8 as pvwattsv8

# Initialize the compute module
pv = pvwattsv8.default('PVWattsNone')

# Load variables from the exported JSON
with open('my_case_pvwattsv8.json', 'r') as f:
  data = json.load(f)

for k, v in data.items():
  if k != 'number_inputs':
    pv.value(k, v)

pv.execute()

aiOverview.content: Trace Software provides advanced integration capabilities for its archelios PRO suite, allowing Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), solar hardware providers, and external platforms to connect their specialized systems directly via APIs.Rather than working in siloed applications, OEM partners utilize these API integrations to streamline the mechanical planning, electrical layout, and component sourcing workflows directly within the web-based simulation environment.Key Archelios API & OEM Integration Use CasesMounting & Mechanical System Selection (OEMs like Enstall & K2 Systems):Through a native API link, users working on a solar layout in archelios PRO can dynamically query an OEM’s database.
